rationale: A wins because it knows where the facts stop. Its best line is the quiet kill switch: "Without an interaction between the two products, this angle is thinner than it looks — confirm it before pitching." B has energy, but "treats 50,000 studios' booking calendars as one data set" and "The AI upgrade boutique fitness startups promised" are not angles; they are facts still waiting to exist.
gaps_in_A: "using aggregated booking data across the network" is not in the update; the facts say booking data, not cross-network aggregation.
"software decides the schedule" oversells the supplied fact. The assistant suggests optimal class times; studios may still ignore it.
"now its AI sits on top of both" makes the ClassPass relationship sound more integrated than the facts support, even though the body later admits this must be confirmed.
gaps_in_B: "treats 50,000 studios' booking calendars as one data set" invents a network-wide data architecture the update never states.
"private-equity ownership" and "answering to private owners" overread the take-private fact; ownership-to-pricing strategy is not supplied.

"The AI upgrade boutique fitness startups promised" invents challengers, promises, and a competitive debate. Requiring "at least one named standalone AI-scheduling competitor" is the tell that the angle is not earned yet.
"adding AI to both" is unsupported. The update says the assistant is for studio scheduling; nothing says it touches ClassPass.
